text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.08% today to $128.12, gaining ground as oil prices firmed and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East kept supply concerns front and center. The spread between U.S. crude ($96.16) and global crude ($113.96) remains wide—a sign of tight supplies globally—while news of a potential U.S.-Iran escalation and continued attacks on tankers near Iran underscored the risk to shipping routes that move a significant portion of the world's oil.

The stock has recovered from a three-day dip that started late last month, and today's move reflects a broader rally in energy as supply fears outweigh the G7's recent pledge to release diesel reserves. Political pressure on South Korea to invest in Alaska LNG and Saudi Aramco's warning that rebuilding global oil stockpiles could take two years both signal that the market expects oil demand and prices to remain supported for some time.
